hints: Notice the shape of the force-extension curve from the origin: the first steep straight-line part is where the wire obeys Hooke's law and would return to original length.
Recall that work done in stretching is the total area under the force against extension curve, so for stretching until it breaks you must include the area from zero extension to breaking extension.
Compare each option by checking two things in order: are elastic then plastic in the correct left-to-right order, and does the work done shading cover the whole area under the curve to breaking?
walkthrough: Look at the force-extension curve for the metal wire stretched to breaking. From the origin the force rises steeply and linearly with extension, then bends over into a long almost flat part before fracture.

The first linear part is the elastic region where deformation is reversible and $F = kx$ holds. Beyond the elastic limit the wire deforms permanently, which is the much larger plastic region leading to breaking.

Work done to stretch the wire is given by $W = \text{area under force-extension graph}$. To stretch until it breaks, this is the total area from $extension = 0$ to the breaking extension, under the whole curve.
Option A shades only the elastic area, and option C shades only the plastic area, so neither shows the total work done. Option B shades the total area but swaps the elastic and plastic labels.
Only the graph with elastic region first, plastic region second, and the whole area shaded satisfies all three labels. This is option D.

options.A: The elastic and plastic regions are in the correct order, but the shaded work done is only the small area up to the elastic limit, not the total area until breaking.
options.B: The shaded area is the total area until breaking, but the region labels are reversed - the initial steep straight part from the origin is the elastic region, not the plastic region.
options.C: The elastic and plastic regions are in the correct order, but the shaded work done starts only after the elastic limit and so omits the work done in the elastic region.
options.D: The initial linear part is labelled elastic region, the later curved part is labelled plastic region, and the shaded area is the total area under the force-extension curve until breaking.
